Total number of questions — 20
Visit of the former Thai Foreign
Minister to North-Eastern States
*381. SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government’s attention has
been drawn to the recent visit of the former
Thai Foreign Minister to North-Eastern
States accompanied by a group of
academicians from South East Asia with a
view to understand India’s Look East
Policy  whereunder they had an
interaction with the students of Guwahati
University;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
delegation broached the conceptualization
of Ganga-Mekong Subarna Bhumi idea;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether Government propose to
conceptualize the said idea by formulating
any policy in this regard; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Unoccupied Government
accommodation in Delhi
*382. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of Government
accommodations that remained unoccupied
during the last five years in Delhi;
(b) what was the revenue loss to
Government on account of unoccupied
houses, year-wise;
(c) whether Government propose to
consider proposal of deducting Licence Fee
and HRA only from the Government
employee, who occupies the flat and not
from his/her spouse, who is also a
Government employee in order to have
higher occupancy of Government
accommodation and higher revenue to
Government; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?

120
Authorized agents under Emigration
Act, 1983
*383. SHRI AMAR SINGH: Will the
Minister of OVERSEAS INDIAN
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the number of authorized agents
under Emigration Act, 1983 in Hyderabad
who have been recruiting labourers for
foreign countries and how many labourers
have been sent by each of them to foreign
countries during the last two years;
(b) whether Government are aware that
a few agents whose licenses have expired
since long have been sending labourers to
foreign countries with connivance of
Protector of Emigrants, Hyderabad;
(c) if so, the names of such recruiting
agents and the number of workers sent by
them after the expiry of their licenses; and
(d) what action Government have taken
against them and the Protector of Emigrants,
Hyderabad?
Defining poverty line
*384. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of URBAN
EMPLOYMENT AND POVERTY
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are
serious flaws in the methodology adopted
by Government in defining poverty line as
it makes very little provision for other
essentials of life like drinking water, shelter
and sanitation;
(b) whether it is a fact that the rate of
decline of poverty since 1973 has been at
dismal 0.81 per cent per annum and the
number of poor stood at about 25 crore in
2004; and
(c) if so, the steps Government propose
to take to include parameters like drinking
water, shelter etc., in the definition of
poverty?
Relaxing of norms under Delhi
Master Plan
*385. SHRI BASHISTHA NARAIN
SINGH: Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether in view of suggestions
received on Delhi Master Plan 2021 and
ground reality, Government have re-looked
at Floor Area Ratio, dwelling units and
height norms for plotted residential
housing;
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor;
(c) the progress made/decision taken on
suggestions to increase number of dwelling
units to four in plots of sizes 100-250 sq.
metres keeping in view the existing reality
of lakhs of such units all over Delhi; and
(d) the status of report of Task Force
on rehabilitation colonies which was to look
into these issues?
Interest rate on Seamens Provident
Fund
*386. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
 Will the Minister of SHIPPING,
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Seamens Provident
Fund attracts less interest than the
Employees Provident Fund;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government are considering
the issue of making the rate of interest
uniform;
(d) if so, the details of the measures
being taken; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?

Long term energy security
2711. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BAL
APTE: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have recently
formulated a nuclear power programme to
provide long-term energy security to the
country based on the indigenous nuclear
fuel resources;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the stage at which it stands at
present?
Reserves of uranium in Orissa
†2712.  SHRI Y ASHWANT SINHA:
   SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL:
 Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a huge reserve
of uranium has been discovered  in the
Vemlagarh and Sayamba region of the
Sundargarh district of Orissa;
(b) whether it is also  a fact that a team
of the scientists is making efforts to discover
and calculate the availability of the huge
potential  of  uranium reserve; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Criteria for setting up of Nuclear
Power Plants
2713. SHRI VARINDER SINGH
BAJWA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) the criteria laid down for setting up
Nuclear Power Plants;
(b) the States which have requested the
Central Government  to set up such  plants;
and
(c) the action taken  by Government in
each case?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

612
Availability of thorium
2714. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the percentage of thorium used  in
the nuclear reactors in the country out of
the total  nuclear fuel;
(b) the potential availability of thorium
in the country as nuclear fuel; and
(c) the steps taken to increase use of
thorium to avoid dependence on uranium
import?
Preservation of fruits in Jammu and
Kashmir
2715. SHRI T.S. BAJWA: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Bhabha Atomic
Research Centre has developed a technique
of long lasting preservation of fruits;
(b) if so, whether this technique has
been tried in Jammu and Kashmir; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Production of coal
†2716. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Coal
India Limited(CIL)  and its subsidaries have
carried out more production  of coal in the
year 2005-06 than 2004-05;
(b) if so, the quantity of coal produced
by the both during the above period,
separately; and
(c) the turnover  of the coal producing
units  during  the above period?
Private investment in coal sector
†2717. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether  it is a fact that Government
have decided to allow the private sector for
making capital investment in the coal  sector;
(b) if so, the facts in this regard; and
(c) by when this decision is likely to be
implemented?
Sliding work force in coal sector
2718. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the work
force in coal industry is sliding  gradually;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) what has been the per employee
production in coal industry during the last
five years, year-wise?
Profits and dividends from CIL and
other subsidiaries
†2719. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA: Will the Minister of
COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Coal
India Limited (CIL) and other subsidiary
coal producing units are expected to earn a
profit of Rs. 7000 crores during 2005-06;

(c) whether the said amount of dividend

Commonwealt Games
2720. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI: Will the Minister of YOUTH
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to
state:
(a) the major steps taken for the hosting
of Commonwealth Games in New Delhi;
(b) whether we have made efforts or
proposed to take measures to train our
sportspersons to perform extraordinary in
Commonwealth Games in North Delhi;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
